newsitem.title: FRANCE: French franc weakens as election worries bite.
newsitem.headline: French franc weakens as election worries bite.

text.p: The French franc weakened against the mark in late trade on worries abroad about the implications of France's parliamentary election for European monetary union.

One Paris trader said London and New York operators were testing the waters to see if they could drive down the franc, which has held steady despite a surprise lead for the opposition Socialist party in the first round of voting on Sunday.
But he said the Bank of France was likely to intervene to prevent any attack on the currency. "It is managing its market very, very well," he said.

In New York, a trader cited comments by National Assembly speaker Philippe Seguin, who said in a newspaper interview that unemployment must be the overriding priority for Europe and it must not stick to niggling conditions for entry to a single currency.
The comments were seen as further evidence France will push for broad membership of Economic and Monetary Union and possibly a weaker euro.
Seguin has been cited as a possible prime minister if the centre-right wins next Sunday's second-round vote, after Prime MInister Alain Juppe said he would step down whoever wins.
The franc was trading at 1700 GMT at 3.3770 per mark, compared to a high earlier in the day of 3.3732.
